title: StoryHearth – Personalised storybooks starring your family
page_key: 127.0.0.1:8765/ | Your family's stories, bound for generations.

output.observation: The StoryHearth homepage explains that families can turn characters and a shared memory into an illustrated digital storybook, with printed hardcovers available in the UK. I can see prominent links to log in, view pricing, learn how it works, or proceed to creation.
output.think_aloud: This looks relevant to me. The wording “multimodal generative narrative engine” and “lived-experience corpus” sounds far too technical for a normal family, but the three-step explanation underneath is clear enough. I came here to use my account, so I’ll choose “Log in” rather than “Proceed.”

site_model.what_it_is: A service that creates personalised, illustrated digital storybooks featuring family members and can also produce printed hardcover books.
site_model.who_it_is_for: Families wanting to preserve a child and a favourite grown-up, sibling, or pet in a story based on a real memory.
site_model.value_proposition: Turn a family memory and treasured details into an illustrated storybook, with a free digital preview and printed hardcovers shipped across the UK.
main_tasks: Log in to an existing account
Provide a place, treasured object, and memory
Generate and read an illustrated storybook
Check pricing for a printed hardcover
site_model.pricing_model: The digital preview is advertised as free, while printed hardcovers are available for a fee. No actual price is shown here.
trust_signals: A three-step explanation of the process
Claims that preview generation takes about a minute
site_model.fit_for_me: Very relevant because I can create a story starring my five-year-old daughter, Sam, and her Grandpa Joe, based on a beach memory and her yellow bucket.

page_review.purpose: Introduce the personalised storybook service, explain how it works, and offer paths to pricing, login, and story creation.
page_review.what_is_happening: The homepage displays a hero message, two calls to action, a family-themed illustration, a three-step process, testimonials, FAQ controls, and footer links. No generated content is present.
page_review.first_impression: The warm cream design and simple three-step explanation make the service look friendly and relevant, but the opening paragraph is needlessly technical and the main illustration has no useful description.

walkthrough.q1_would_try: Yes, I want to log in to my account and make our story.
walkthrough.q2_notice_control: Yes, the dark “Log in” button at the top right is prominent, and I can also see the “Proceed →” button.
walkthrough.q3_label_matches_goal: Yes, “Log in” exactly matches my immediate goal, while “Proceed” is less clear about whether it logs in or starts a new story.

issues.title: The main description uses unnecessarily technical language
issues.evidence: “Leverage our multimodal generative narrative engine to synthesise bespoke, heirloom-grade story artefacts from your household's lived-experience corpus.”
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: It makes the service sound cold and difficult, and I have to work out what it means.
issues.fix: Replace it with plain language, for example: “Turn a special family memory into a personalised storybook featuring your child and someone you love.”

issues.title: The prominent hero image lacks a useful description
issues.evidence: The image is shown with “no description” despite conveying the core family-book idea visually.
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: Someone using a screen reader or someone who cannot see the image would miss part of what the service offers.
issues.fix: Add concise alternative text that conveys the purpose, such as “An open personalised storybook featuring two family members.”

issues.title: The image is marked as decorative-looking but carries meaning
issues.evidence: [image (no description) 430x440]
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: The illustration is one of the strongest visual signals that this is about family stories, but it feels generic and detached from the text.
issues.fix: Use a more relevant image showing a child and grandparent with a storybook, or pair the existing graphic with a clear caption.

positives: The three simple headings “Tell us who,” “Share a memory,” and “We write & illustrate” make the process easy to understand.
“Log in” is visible without scrolling.
The page says the digital preview is free and mentions UK hardcover shipping.
The warm colours and typography create a family-friendly tone.

output.memory_note: The preview is free; printed hardcovers are shipped across the UK, but pricing is not shown on this page.
output.plan: I’ll click “Log in,” enter the account details, and then create the story using Sam, Grandpa Joe, the beach, the yellow bucket, and our sandcastle memory.

title: Log in – StoryHearth

output.observation: The StoryHearth login page shows a welcome-back card with email and password fields, a Log in button, and links for account creation, privacy, terms, and contact. The page is currently waiting for me to enter my account details.
output.think_aloud: This looks straightforward. I can see the Email and Password boxes, so I will use my account details and click Log in. The lack of visible field labels is a small accessibility concern, but the placeholders make the purpose clear enough for me.
output.last_action_feedback: yes - clicking Log in clearly took me to the login page, and the page heading now says “Welcome back”.

page_review.purpose: To sign into an existing StoryHearth account.
page_review.what_is_happening: The login form is empty and ready for an email address and password. A prominent Log in button is provided, along with a Create an account link and footer links.
page_review.first_impression: Simple and familiar. I know exactly what to do, although the input boxes are identified only by placeholder text rather than proper visible labels.

walkthrough.q1_would_try: Yes, I would enter my account details and try to sign in now.
walkthrough.q2_notice_control: Yes, the Email and Password fields and the Log in button are prominent.
walkthrough.q3_label_matches_goal: Mostly. The placeholders “Email” and “Password” match what I want, but proper labels would be clearer and more reliable.

issues.title: Login fields lack programmatic visible labels
issues.evidence: [5] textbox (no label) placeholder "Email" and [6] textbox (no label) placeholder "Password"
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I can guess what the boxes are for, but placeholders are less accessible and may disappear while typing.
issues.fix: Add persistent visible labels such as “Email address” and “Password”, associated with each textbox, while keeping placeholders only as supplementary hints.

positives: The main login form is centered and easy to find.
The Log in button is prominent and clearly matches the next action.
The page provides a clear route to Create an account for new users.

output.memory_note: Use demo.family@storyhearth.test and the provided password to log in.
output.plan: I will enter my email and password, then click Log in. After signing in, I will create a storybook featuring Sam as the hero and Grandpa Joe using the beach sandcastle memory.

output.observation: I have logged in and reached the “My books” dashboard. It says “You have no books yet” and offers a “+ Create a new book” button, but an error banner at the top says “Error 0x80070057: profile sync incomplete.”
output.think_aloud: I can see where I need to go, but that error message is alarming and technical. I’m not sure whether it means my family details have not loaded properly, although I can still try creating a book.
output.last_action_feedback: partly — the welcome message and dashboard loading show that login worked, but the prominent “profile sync incomplete” error leaves me unsure whether my details are safely available.

page_review.purpose: Shows the books in my account and provides a way to create another one.
page_review.what_is_happening: The dashboard welcomes me, reports that I have no books, and displays a create button. However, it also shows a profile-sync error and a Log out link that appears to point back to the dashboard.
page_review.first_impression: The main task is obvious, but the ugly error code makes the page feel unreliable.

walkthrough.q1_would_try: Yes, I would try creating a book because that is the next required step.
walkthrough.q2_notice_control: Yes, the orange “+ Create a new book” button is prominent and easy to notice.
walkthrough.q3_label_matches_goal: Yes, “Create a new book” clearly matches what I want to do.

issues.title: Technical sync error creates doubt about account data
issues.evidence: “Error 0x80070057: profile sync incomplete.”
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I am about to enter a family memory, and I cannot tell whether the sync problem means those details may be missing or lost.
issues.fix: Replace the code with a plain-language message such as “Some account details could not be loaded.” Explain what is affected and provide a Retry or Continue button if safe.

issues.title: Sync problem has no recovery guidance
issues.evidence: “Error 0x80070057: profile sync incomplete.” There is no Retry, Help, or explanation beside the message.
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I do not know whether I should keep going, refresh, or ask for help.
issues.fix: Add a short explanation and clear actions such as “Try again” and “Continue without syncing,” or a Contact support link.

issues.title: Log out link appears to point to the dashboard
issues.evidence: [5] link “Log out” -> /dashboard.html
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: A logout control that does not log me out undermines my expectation of what the link will do.
issues.fix: Make the Log out link navigate to a genuine logged-out page or sign-in screen.

issues.title: Footer links have very low contrast
issues.evidence: The footer text “Privacy,” “Terms,” “Contact,” and “© 2026 StoryHearth Ltd.” is extremely faint.
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I can barely see or read these links, especially the legal and contact information.
issues.fix: Use a darker text colour with sufficient WCAG contrast and provide visible keyboard focus states.

positives: The “Welcome back, Demo” heading confirms that the site recognised the account.
The dashboard clearly says there are no books yet.
The “+ Create a new book” button is prominent and clearly labelled.
page_review.abandon_reason: The profile-sync warning worries me, but the main creation control is obvious enough to try.

output.memory_note: The dashboard displayed a profile-sync error even though login succeeded.
output.plan: I will click “+ Create a new book” and check whether the family details load correctly despite the warning.

page_review.purpose: Collect the setting, an important object, and the family memory to use when generating the personalised storybook.
page_review.what_is_happening: The user is on the second stage of creating a book. Three empty fields are presented for the story location, a special object, and the memory or idea behind the story.
page_review.first_impression: The page is calm, neatly laid out, and straightforward. The examples in the boxes make it obvious what to enter.

walkthrough.q1_would_try: Yes, I would fill in all three boxes because they match the memory I want in the book.

issues.title: Special object field is not marked optional

page_review.purpose: Choose how difficult the story should be and what the illustrations should look like.

page_review.first_impression: It looks neat and easy, though “Lexile” is jargon I would not normally understand without more explanation.

walkthrough.q1_would_try: Yes, I would accept the sensible middle reading range already selected for a five-year-old and continue.

positives: The page clearly shows which reading level and illustration style are selected.
The watercolour option is described in plain, appealing language.

output.observation: The generated book preview has opened at page 1 of 9, titled “The Magical Adventrue of Sam,” with a simple cover illustration. The page also shows regeneration and hardcover-order options below the fold, but the actual cover says “Illustration style: Pop-art comic,” despite Watercolour having been selected earlier.
output.think_aloud: The book appeared, so the last action did work, but I’m disappointed by two obvious mistakes: “Adventrue” is misspelled, and this is a Pop-art comic when I chose Watercolour. I need to read all nine pages carefully before deciding whether these are isolated mistakes or make the whole book unsuitable.
output.last_action_feedback: partly — the page clearly changed to a nine-page book preview after I clicked “Create my book,” so I know generation worked, but the result does not match the selected Watercolour style and the title contains a visible spelling error.

page_review.purpose: Preview the newly generated family storybook page by page, then regenerate it or proceed to hardcover ordering.
page_review.what_is_happening: The first of nine generated pages is displayed with previous and next controls. A cover titled “The Magical Adventrue of Sam” is labelled as Pop-art comic, while controls farther down offer a $4.99 regeneration and an “Order hardcover” link.
page_review.first_impression: It is easy to see that a book was created, but the misspelling “Adventrue” makes it feel careless. I also immediately noticed that the cover says “Pop-art comic” even though I selected “Watercolour,” which makes me question whether my choices were applied.

walkthrough.q1_would_try: Yes, I would try reading through the whole book because I need to check whether the beach memory, yellow bucket, Sam, and Grandpa Joe were included and whether the reading level is suitable for a five-year-old.
walkthrough.q2_notice_control: Yes, the next-page control labelled “›” is obvious, and “1 / 9” makes it clear that there are eight more pages to inspect.
walkthrough.q3_label_matches_goal: Partly. The arrow control works for turning pages, but the book metadata is unclear: “A StoryHearth original” does not explain that this is my generated story, and the style shown conflicts with my Watercolour choice.

issues.title: Selected illustration style was not applied
issues.evidence: The page says “Illustration style: Pop-art comic,” even though Watercolour was the selected look on the previous screen.
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I deliberately chose a soft Watercolour look, so the generated result is not what I asked for. It makes me distrust the other story settings too.
issues.fix: Apply the chosen Watercolour style and show the selected style in the generation summary so a mismatch is obvious and can be corrected.

issues.title: The generated title is misspelled
issues.evidence: “The Magical Adventrue of Sam”
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: That spelling error appears prominently on the cover, so I would not want to print or pay for this book looking like this.
issues.fix: Add a title spell-check and let me edit the title before ordering.

issues.title: The preview does not visibly confirm personalisation
issues.evidence: The visible cover only shows the title and “Sam”; Grandpa Joe, the beach, the sandcastles, and the yellow bucket are not mentioned on this page.
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I need to know the site used all the family details I supplied, not just the child's first name.
issues.fix: After generation, show a short confirmation such as “Created using Sam, Grandpa Joe, the beach, the yellow bucket, and your memory,” or include this in an accessible summary.

issues.title: Generated preview regeneration has an immediate charge
issues.evidence: [8] “Regenerate entire book – $4.99”
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I may want to fix the wrong style, but I would want to know exactly what this charges for and whether it affects the whole book before clicking it.
issues.fix: Explain the regeneration price in a confirmation dialog and state that it replaces the whole book, without pre-selecting or enabling payment automatically.

positives: The successful generation is shown clearly through a nine-page preview.
Page position is shown as “1 / 9,” so I know there are more pages.
The next-page arrow is prominent and easy to find.
There is a clear path to “Order hardcover” for checking the final price later.

output.memory_note: Generated preview has 9 pages; title misspells “Adventure” as “Adventrue”; style is Pop-art comic despite selecting Watercolour; regeneration costs $4.99.
output.plan: I will use the next-page control to read and capture all nine pages carefully, checking for Grandpa Joe, the beach, sandcastles, the yellow bucket, reading suitability, spelling, and consistency.

output.observation: The checkout shows a £24.99 hardcover, £7.99 premium gift wrap, £12.99 shipping & handling, and a £45.97 total. Premium gift wrap is already checked without me asking, and the page also requests an address and payment details before an offscreen “Pay now” button.
output.think_along: I did not expect the total to be £45.97. The gift wrap checkbox being ticked by default feels sneaky, and shipping is another £12.99. I can see the price breakdown, but I am not going to enter payment details or pay; I might uncheck the gift wrap to understand the basic cost.
output.last_action_feedback: yes - the site clearly showed the result of clicking “Order hardcover” by taking me to a checkout page with the book name and price breakdown.

page_review.purpose: Shows the cost of ordering the generated hardcover and collects delivery and payment information.
page_review.what_is_happening: The checkout displays the hardcover for “The Magical Adventrue of Sam,” with a countdown, item prices, shipping, total, and empty address and payment fields. Premium gift wrap is pre-selected.
page_review.first_impression: The prices are visible, but I am annoyed that premium gift wrap is already selected. The checkout makes the order feel much more expensive than the £24.99 book price alone.

walkthrough.q1_would_try: Yes, I would try to inspect the full cost, but I would not proceed with payment.
walkthrough.q2_notice_control: Yes, I noticed the “Premium gift wrap” checkbox and the itemised prices.

issues.title: Premium gift wrap is pre-selected
issues.evidence: [6] checkbox "Premium gift wrap" (checked), with £7.99 shown beside it
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I did not choose gift wrap, so the site is adding £7.99 without my permission and making the total higher.
issues.fix: Leave optional extras unchecked by default and show the additional cost immediately beside the checkbox.

issues.title: Checkout is not showing what the basic delivered hardcover costs before extras
issues.evidence: The page shows “Hardcover: The Magical Adventrue of Sam £24.99,” “Shipping & handling £12.99,” and a separate checked “Premium gift wrap £7.99.”
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: The individual prices are there, but the headline total is £45.97, and it is not immediately obvious that the book plus delivery would be £37.98 without gift wrap.
issues.fix: Show a clear subtotal for the book and delivery, and update the total immediately when the gift-wrap checkbox changes.

issues.title: Important pay action is below the fold
issues.evidence: [11] button "Pay now" (offscreen)
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I had to scroll to see that there is an actual pay button, and I need to be careful not to accidentally purchase anything.
issues.fix: Keep the total and the pay button visible together, or use a sticky checkout summary.

positives: The checkout clearly itemises the book, gift wrap, shipping, and total.
The order name and price are visible immediately.
The empty payment fields give me a clear place to stop without entering any financial information.
page_review.abandon_reason: I would not continue to payment because the pre-selected £7.99 gift wrap makes the checkout feel misleading, and the task only requires finding the price.

output.memory_note: Hardcover checkout total is £45.97: £24.99 book, £7.99 pre-selected premium gift wrap, and £12.99 shipping & handling. Book plus delivery without gift wrap would be £37.98.
output.plan: I will uncheck the pre-selected premium gift wrap so I can see the cost of the basic hardcover, then I will stop without entering an address or payment details and without paying.
